title: Checks, captures, and threats in 20–30 seconds
subtitle: Real positions from {{username}} — the solution is not shown here.
step1Body: Before you move in a non-trivial position, ask: do I have a useful check? If you already have a candidate, what check does your opponent have right after?
step1Checklist2: After your candidate, imagine your opponent’s most awkward check
step2Body: What can you capture now? If you capture, what is the recapture and what stays attacked or hanging?
step3Body: What is the strongest threat for each side? Not the prettiest — the one that changes material balance or king safety.
step4Body: Imagine your opponent knows your idea. Look for their most uncomfortable reply — forced capture, check, intermezzo — not the natural move you expect.
step5Body: Only then confirm your move. At your level, a hostile one- or two-move line matters more than a long pretty variation you did not refute.
step5Checklist1: Does my move survive my opponent’s best forced reply?
step5Checklist2: Did I consider checks and captures before a quiet plan?
